issues.description: URL-rewriter function lacks a stated contract for its inputs and outputs.
issues.detail: use_koji_url_only treats every input as either a coreos-pool URL or a parseable NEVRA-bearing URL, but never states the precondition. If a URL lacks a recognized arch, extract_arch_from_url returns None and the function silently emits a malformed URL containing 'None'. State the precondition or reject violators explicitly.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url postcondition allows None to flow into URL construction.
issues.detail: The function's postcondition is 'returns arch or None', but the sole caller assumes a string. This is a classic LSP-style contract mismatch at the call boundary: the caller strengthens what the callee promises. Either narrow the callee (raise on miss) or have the caller handle None and skip/error.

issues.description: noarch packages violate the implicit arch invariant of the koji path scheme.
issues.detail: The koji canonical path is /latest/{arch}/Packages/{letter}/{nevra}. noarch RPMs are resolved via --arch noarch and their filenames end in .noarch.rpm, yet extract_arch_from_url only matches four arches. A noarch URL will either get a wrong arch from elsewhere in the path or None. The ADT must include 'noarch' as a legal arch.

issues.description: Leaky abstraction: koji path layout hardcoded as string concatenation inside the rewriter.
issues.detail: The canonical koji path structure (/latest/{arch}/Packages/{first-letter}/{nevra}) is an external contract owned by Fedora koji, not by this script. Encoding it inline as string splits and joins leaks that layout throughout the module. A small build_koji_url(nevra, arch) helper would localize the contract and make future koji layout changes a one-line edit.

issues.description: nevra[0].lower() assumes ASCII-alphabetic first character without stating it.
issues.detail: The koji Packages directory uses the lowercase first letter of the package name. The code takes nevra[0], but nevra is a filename like '389-ds-base-...'; a digit-leading package puts the file under '/3/' which koji does honor, so this likely works, but the invariant ('first char of package name, lowercased') is unstated and fragile. Document it or extract package name from NEVRA properly.

issues.description: SPEC-MISSING on the race condition acknowledged in the PR description.
issues.detail: The PR description names a real correctness hazard: URLs are crafted before coreos-koji-tagger actually tags. This is a precondition on the consumer ('lockfile is consumed only after tagging completes') that lives nowhere in code. At minimum, a module-level docstring should state this contract so future maintainers don't reuse the function in a context where the precondition doesn't hold.

review.summary: The patch is a reasonable workaround for a DNF5 bug, but it introduces a small URL-rewriting ADT without stating its contract. The precondition (every non-pool URL contains a recognized arch token and a NEVRA-shaped filename) and postcondition (always returns a valid koji URL) are implicit, and the None-return path from extract_arch_from_url silently produces malformed URLs. noarch is a legal arch in this domain and is unhandled. The koji path layout is also leaking through string concatenation rather than living behind a single helper. None of this blocks merge, but the module boundary should be tightened before this code outlives its current single caller.
